The title and summary present the codebook as settled, but the specification records that its worst boundary is unresolved after seven attempts: `observation`/`principle` accounts for 42% of all disagreement on real documents and is described as irreducible rather than ill-defined. An entry on the codebook that omits its known irreducible boundary overstates it.

The exemplars are named as part of the required shape of every definition but no assertion carries one. The document's own evidence says concretely-described features outperform interpretive ones, which makes the exemplars load-bearing rather than decorative.

Nineteen separation rules are mentioned; four are stated. The unstated ones include `background`/`event`, which uniquely instructs deciding from surrounding context rather than the sentence alone -- an exception to the surface-test principle the rest of the codebook rests on.
